provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Generator mechanism: in canonical form, a tridiagonal band runs along the main diagonal of an n x n input. The band has diagonal colours diag[i%L] and off-diagonal colours offdiag[(i+1)%L], with L equal to 2 or 3. The output is 2n x 2n and holds the same band continued from the top-left anchor to the far corner. When flop is set, both grids are mirrored left-right (common.flop reverses each row; fixture pair 3 confirms this). In that case the band lies on the anti-diagonal and the input sits in the top-right corner of the output.

The factory maps the two canonical anchor corners (TL for a main-diagonal band, TR for an anti-diagonal band) through the D4 transform: optional row reversal, then clockwise rotations acting on corner bits. Whichever image is a TL/BR corner becomes ANCHOR_MAIN, the anchor used when the visible band lies on the main diagonal. The other becomes ANCHOR_ANTI. The background constant is palette[0].

The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates:
1. It classifies the band as main or anti by checking which diagonal is fully non-background.
2. It picks the anchor corner and the extension direction (dr, dc) pointing away from that corner.
3. It finds the smallest diagonal shift p with g[r][c] == g[r+p*dr][c+p*dc] on the overlap. The 2D check covers diagonal and off-diagonal runs together. By Fine-Wilf with n>=5, p is a true period of the infinite band.
4. It builds a 2H x 2W canvas with the input stamped at the anchor corner. Every other cell is stepped back toward the anchor by (p*dr, p*dc) until it lands inside the input footprint, and that colour is copied. If it leaves the footprint on the anchor side, it stays background.

Off-band cells keep their row-column offset while stepping, so they resolve to background. The extension direction is fixed by the episode's D4 rather than guessed from the query. This matters because a visible main-diagonal band can be anchored at either TL or BR depending on the transform, and the band phase (diag[0] at the anchor) makes those two answers differ.
draft_notes.limitations:
Constructor/solver defect for host review: the archived solver and the rule text treat the anti-diagonal case with a vertical flip, which anchors the input at the bottom-left of the output. The generator instead applies a horizontal flop, which anchors the input at the top-right and extends toward the bottom-left. The two agree only when n is a multiple of the band period, as in fixture pair 3 (n=8, period 2) and the test (n=10, period 2). For fresh scenes such as n=5 or 7 with period 2, or n not divisible by 3 with period 3, the archived solver differs from the generator labels. This factory follows the generator; all supplied fixtures are consistent with it.

The extension direction comes from the d4 argument, not from demonstrations. This is valid because D4 is fixed per episode and canonical anchors are fixed by orientation. Orientation detection assumes diagonal colours are never the background (palette[0]), which the generator guarantees. Rectangular grids are handled mechanically (2H x 2W output, min-dimension diagonal test), but the constructor only produces square grids of size 5 to 10. No tests have been run.
draft_notes.host_review: Keep constructor labels and original direct factory; document synthetic convention: anti band uses top-right anchor in native orientation, whereas archived opposite-anchor reading can differ at nonmultiple sizes. Gate independently extracts diagonal/off-diagonal periods and evaluates all four combinations of main/anti top-versus-bottom phase. Demonstrations only constrain their own visible axis; require same-query prediction agreement. Period-multiple queries may pass without a phase-discriminating demo. No constructor or label change.
draft_notes.semantic_draft_review: Opus5.5 subscription CLI reviewed; episode evidence implemented without per-pair narrowing or fixture overrides.
